clue.text: The new wife happily going into prison

parts.note: a newly married woman is a bride
well, as in things going well, means happily

explanation.surface: A newly married woman is cheerfully on her way to jail.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIDEWELL was a London prison, and the name became a general word for a house of correction.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridewell is an old word for a jail or house of correction, after the London institution of that name.

clue.text: Flashy and boozy airman?

parts.note: the RAF is the Royal Air Force, so an airman belongs to it
a fish is one who drinks like a fish, a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: A showy pilot who likes a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom 'drink like a fish' means drink heavily, so a boozy person is a fish here.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffish means rakishly showy and a bit disreputable.

clue.text: A fall in the German production of kitchen equipment

indicators.note: the shower sits inside the German article

parts.note: der is a German word for the
a fall of water from the sky is rain

explanation.surface: A tumble by a German leads to making something for the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A fall' suggests a tumble but means a fall of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A rack or colander where washed dishes or food drip dry.

clue.text: He'll hit the drink with little hesitation!

parts.note: wallop is British slang for beer
er is the small sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: He will knock back the booze without pausing much.
explanation.walkthrough: WALLOP is British slang for beer; 'hit the drink' sounds like drinking hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wallops is a person who strikes hard, a thumper.

clue.text: The most impoverished look to the West

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or behold
taken as written

explanation.surface: The poorest gaze westward.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowest here means poorest, at the bottom in rank or wealth.

clue.text: They will be suspended at Christmas

definitions.text: They will be suspended at Christmas

parts.words: They will be suspended at Christmas
parts.note: items hung up by the fireplace on Christmas Eve for presents, not people barred from work

explanation.definitionFit: Children hang up long socks at Christmas for gifts to be put in them.

clue.text: Get rid of pollution and get rich

definitions.meaning: to clear away dirt and waste
to make a big profit, an idiom

explanation.surface: Clean the environment and make a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to clear away dirt and, colloquially, to make a large profit.

clue.text: A French aim is to include a tree variety not listed

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: the word for aim includes, or encloses, the rearranged letters

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

indicators.note: a variety of something is a different form, so the letters of tree are rearranged

explanation.surface: A French goal is to plant a type of tree that is not on the register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' rearranges TREE to TERE, and 'to include' puts TERE inside END.
explanation.definitionFit: Not entered means not recorded on a register or list.

clue.text: None ran around much in retirement to get bunting

parts.note: O, the figure zero, stands for none

indicators.note: the word ran goes round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word for much is read backwards

parts.note: a lot means much

explanation.surface: Nobody runs about much once they have retired, but they still get flags out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' reverses LOT to TOL, and 'around' puts TOL inside RAN. 'bunting' looks like flags but is the bird family.
explanation.definitionFit: The ortolan is a small European songbird of the bunting family, once a gourmet delicacy.

clue.text: Kind of a lie taking in the female

indicators.note: the first pieces take in, or enclose, the letter for female

parts.note: a fable is a made-up story, a lie
F is the standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A sort of falsehood involving a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' reads as 'sort of' in the surface but is the adjective meaning friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Affable means pleasant and friendly, so a kind person is affable.

clue.text: Hold the small child in inane fashion

indicators.note: the abbreviation for child sits inside the rearranged letters
to fashion something is to shape it anew, so the letters of inane are reworked

parts.note: CH is the short form of child

explanation.surface: Grip the little one in a silly way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' rearranges INANE to ENAIN and 'in' puts CH inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchain is to bind with chains, so to restrain or keep captive.

clue.text: Traffic indicators

parts.note: roadside boards pointing the way for drivers, though the phrase could suggest car indicator lights

explanation.definitionFit: Roadside posts with arms show drivers the directions and distances to places.

clue.text: Dicky tarried, getting more behind-hand

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for unsound or shaky, so the letters of tarried are disordered

explanation.surface: A man called Dicky lingered and so fell further behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name but is British slang for shaky, here an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardier means later or slower, so further behind time.

clue.text: View this as a theatrical pose

definitions.meaning: an opinion or way of looking at something
a striking bodily posture, as when an actor strikes one

explanation.surface: Consider this a bit of stage posturing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a settled opinion and a dramatic posture adopted for effect.

clue.text: The cost of an attack

definitions.meaning: a rush forward against an enemy, as by cavalry

explanation.surface: The price of launching an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a fee demanded and a headlong assault on an enemy.

clue.text: A bar snack

parts.note: a snack sold in bar form, not something eaten in a pub

explanation.definitionFit: This sweet confection is commonly sold in bars.

clue.text: The earthy forecaster!

parts.note: earthy suggests coarse, but here it means one who foretells the future from earth

explanation.definitionFit: This diviner reads the future from patterns in earth or soil.

clue.text: Wearing, so may be ignored

indicators.note: the letters of ignored may be something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: It is tiresome, so it might be overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' suggests tiring, but here it means wearing away.
explanation.definitionFit: Eroding is wearing away gradually, as water does to rock.

clue.text: Bearing with a dreadful crisis caused by bloomers

parts.note: N, north, is a compass bearing

indicators.note: a dreadful crisis is in a bad state, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Coping with a terrible emergency caused by gaffes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' suggests blunders or knickers but means flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Daffodils and their kin are spring flowers, and a bloomer is a flowering plant.

clue.text: A friendly gathering-or quite the opposite?

parts.note: a social is an informal party or get-together

explanation.surface: Is this a party, or is it the reverse?
explanation.walkthrough: Read as one word, the A becomes a prefix meaning not, so the answer is the opposite of sociable.
explanation.definitionFit: Asocial means avoiding company, the reverse of a party mood.

clue.text: Rise arranged for a number in transport

indicators.note: the number is placed inside the word for transport

parts.note: to send someone is to transport them with delight
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Lifting has been organised for a group travelling by vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' looks like vehicles but means to delight, SEND; C, a Roman hundred, goes inside it after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to go up or climb.

clue.text: In short cannot even find a place to eat

parts.note: can't is the shortened form of cannot
e'en is the poetic shortened form of even

explanation.surface: In brief, there is nowhere at all to dine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In short' tells you to shorten both words: CAN'T and E'EN.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen is a cafeteria at a workplace or school.

clue.text: An uplifting perfume now being developed

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting up a word turns it upside down, so An is read backwards

parts.note: a scent is a perfume

explanation.surface: An inspiring fragrance is in the works.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means coming into being, just starting to grow.

clue.text: Cold remains-simple stuff

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
ash is what remains after burning
mere means simple or nothing more than

explanation.surface: Chilly leftovers are plain fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuff' is the old sense of woven fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is a fine wool fabric, and stuff is an old word for woven cloth.

clue.text: Tottered as a result of wound

definitions.meaning: wrapped round a spool, as thread or line

explanation.surface: He staggered because he was injured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' rhymes with sound here, the past of wind, not an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both staggered and wound onto a reel.

clue.text: Build up the head's standing

parts.note: to erect a building is to build it up
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Bolster the headteacher's reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is a headland, NESS, not a headteacher; 'standing' is the state of standing upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Being upright, or standing straight, is the state described.

clue.text: " they mean when they cry Liberty." Milton (Sonnets)

definitions.text: " they mean when they cry Liberty." Milton (Sonnets)

parts.words: " they mean when they cry Liberty." Milton (Sonnets)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from a Milton sonnet, where the missing first word is unrestrained freedom mistaken for liberty

explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Milton's sonnet on the reception of his divorce tracts: what the crowd want, he says, is not liberty but freedom without restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word means unbridled freedom or permissiveness, contrasted by Milton with true liberty.

clue.text: American woman the editor went along with

parts.note: her is a pronoun for a woman
ED is the short form of editor

explanation.surface: A US lady accompanied the newspaper boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To usher someone is to escort them, going along with them to a seat or place.

clue.text: For the athlete who's a real swinger!

definitions.text: For the athlete who's a real swinger!

parts.words: For the athlete who's a real swinger!
parts.note: a swinger usually means a lively socialite, but here it is a gymnast swinging from a bar high up

explanation.definitionFit: This circus bar hangs on two ropes for acrobats to swing from.

clue.text: Mark ingested a peculiar mixture

indicators.note: the letters of ingested a are mixed up in an odd way

explanation.surface: Mark swallowed a strange concoction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name but is a verb meaning to label.
explanation.definitionFit: To designate something is to mark it out or indicate it.
